opportunities.accessMethod: Not published in the open-data service. The text exists only on individual list-entry web pages, reachable one document at a time via the `hyperlink` field.
opportunities.licence: unknown for the description text; the spatial data is OGL v3.0
opportunities.attributionRequirement: Contains Historic England information © Historic England (for the open data)
opportunities.expectedGeographicGain: none — same places, more detail about them
opportunities.runtimeCost: one document retrieval per record; ~400,000 nationally
opportunities.operationalRisk: Retrieving hundreds of thousands of pages from a public website is a bulk-use decision with terms, rate and politeness consequences that Whilom cannot settle from the outside.
evidence: The NHLE FeatureServer publishes 11 layers with 23 distinct fields between them; none is a description and every date field records an act of the state.
All 247 feature services published by Historic England were enumerated; none carries list-entry description text.
historicengland.org.uk returned HTTP 403 to a non-browser request — including for robots.txt — so even the crawl policy could not be established, let alone bulk terms.
This is the single largest temporal opportunity available and it is blocked on access, not on engineering.

opportunities.accessMethod: The same ArcGIS FeatureServer Whilom already ingests, without the regional envelope
opportunities.attributionRequirement: Contains Historic England information © Historic England. Contains OS data © Crown copyright
opportunities.expectedGeographicGain: England-wide, from one Yorkshire band to the whole country
opportunities.conflictRate: unchanged per record; the same pipeline and the same matcher
opportunities.runtimeCost: 17× the current corpus through an already-proven pipeline
opportunities.operationalRisk: The scale ladder has been proven to 25,000 records, not 400,000. Every map gate, the cluster aggregation and the coverage-truthfulness model were tuned against 23,151 places. This is a batch of its own, not a flag.
evidence: Same licence, same stable identifiers, same adapter: no new access or licensing question at all.
By a wide margin the largest geographic gain available, and the only one requiring no new source.

opportunities.accessMethod: SPARQL, joined on P1216 (NHLE list entry)
opportunities.expectedGeographicGain: none — enriches places Whilom already holds
opportunities.conflictRate: low; events are usually different facts rather than competing dates
opportunities.unhandledRate: 6 of 41 rejected as not about the place
opportunities.operationalRisk: Requires a governed event vocabulary. Several dated event types describe a modern investigation rather than the place, and importing them blindly would date a Bronze Age barrow to 2015.
evidence: 33 distinct dated event types measured regionally; 26 governed as evidence, 7 refused by name.
Semantics are genuinely distinct: demolition, conflagration, slighting and licence to crenellate are four different claims and must not collapse into one generic date.

opportunities.operationalRisk: One of the five terms is broader than any single Whilom period. "Middle Ages" spans three registry periods, and narrowing it to the best-overlapping one would invent precision the source did not give.
evidence: 5 distinct period items measured; classified BROADER_THAN_REGISTRY, CONTROLLED_ALIAS, CONTROLLED_ALIAS, DIRECT_REGISTRY_MATCH, DIRECT_REGISTRY_MATCH.
The only genuinely controlled period vocabulary either source offers — everything else is a word read out of a name.

opportunities.source: Wikidata — start time (P580) and point in time (P585)
opportunities.operationalRisk: The semantics are ambiguous by design. P580 on a heritage item may mean the structure began, or the organisation occupying it began, or a designation began — and 28 places is not enough evidence to settle which, per item, without reading them.
evidence: 21 places carry P580 and 7 carry P585 regionally.
Batch 11 established that a property must be imported for what it means, not for the fact it holds a date. These two do not have one settled meaning on this class of item.
